hint.totalEarned: Total coins customers received in the selected period (top-ups, promotions, order rewards).
hint.totalSpent: Total coins customers spent in the selected period (paying with coins, redeeming gift cards).
hint.netDifference: Coins earned minus coins spent. A positive number means customers are accumulating faster than they spend — the pool of unspent coins is growing.
hint.vsPrevious: Compared with the period immediately before, of the SAME LENGTH. Viewing the last 30 days means the previous period is the 30 days before that.
hint.trend: Roughly how much it rises or falls per period, estimated by fitting a straight line through the bars. Indicative only, not a forecast.
hint.r2: How closely the trend line follows the real data, from 0 to 1. Near 1 means a close, trustworthy fit. Below 0.3 the bars are too erratic for the trend number to mean much.
hint.pValue: The chance this trend number is just random noise. Below 0.05 is considered trustworthy.
hint.transactions: Number of coin transactions in this time bucket, counting both additions and deductions.

slope.quick: How much does it rise or fall each period? Positive (+) is up, negative (-) is down.
slope.body: The average rate of change from one bar to the next. For example +39,286/month: each new month the figure climbs by roughly 39,286. It is an average estimate, not a promise about the future — check R² and p before trusting it.

r2.quick: Does the line follow reality? Closer to 1 is trustworthy; below 0.1 is worthless.
r2.body: Real data jumps around while the system draws one straight line. R² says how much of the truth that line captures. Below 0.1 the line and the data go their separate ways. 0.1–0.3 very weak. 0.3–0.6 moderate. Above 0.6 clear and closely fitted. R² 0.02 means it captures just 2%.

pValue.quick: Could this just be luck? It must be below {{alpha}} to be trusted.
pValue.body: Measures whether this is a real trend or pure chance. p = 0.772 means a 77.2% chance it is luck — do not trust it. p = 0.001 means only 0.1% is luck, so the trend genuinely exists.

band.quick: How precisely is the line placed? A narrow band is precise — but still check R².
band.body: This is the margin of error: 95% of the time the true line sits inside the shaded area. Important: the band describes only WHERE the line is, not how well that line describes the data. More buckets automatically narrow the band, so you can easily meet a narrow band around a line with a very low R² — precisely placed, yet explaining nothing. To judge trustworthiness, read R². A band splaying wide means the data swings too much to say whether it is rising or falling.

hidden.term: Why is the trend line sometimes missing?
hidden.quick: The rule is: better to say nothing than to guess.
hidden.body: Both conditions must hold before a line is drawn: p < {{alpha}} (not luck) and R² ≥ {{minR2}} (it explains at least something). Without the R² condition, large samples push through lines that are "statistically correct" yet explain only a few percent. Note that few buckets are not disqualified automatically — the test already accounts for sample size, so fewer points simply demand a tighter fit.

trend.label: Trend
trend.weakHint: Low R² — trend is not reliable

verdict.notSignificant: No clear trend — this number could just be random noise.
verdict.negligible: Statistically different from zero, but the line explains too little to be useful.
verdict.weak: There is a trend, but the data is noisy, so treat it as a rough guide only.
